# Update engine-repo `core/README.md` staff description to the two-type model

## Problem statement

The `core/README.md` in the Tableau-Card-Engine (engine) repository still describes Main Street staff with the superseded single-type framing ("staff cards expand hand capacity with ongoing costs"). Staff are now two types — business staff and management-company staff — and only management-company staff grant hand capacity.

## Impact

Players reading the engine's documentation get a clearer picture of how Main Street's staff system works.

## Users

- Developers using the engine who reference the README for game-specific features.
- Contributors reviewing Main Street's integration with the engine.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/README.md`'s Main Street row no longer states that staff cards expand hand capacity as their defining role; it names the two staff types (business staff and management-company staff) and clarifies that only management-company staff grant hand capacity.
2. The change is merged on the engine repository's `dev` branch and the submodule pin is advanced in this repo (tce-main-street) when that is the normal practice (separate pnpm/npm bump if required).
3. Any engine-repository work item that tracks the change is referenced here.

## Constraints

- The file lives in the separate Tableau-Card-Engine repository (`core/` submodule, `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), so the change must be made there, not in this repo.
- Follow the established practice for submodule pin updates in this repository.
- Write in UK English.

## Existing state

Line 350 of `core/README.md` (Main Street row in the example-games table):
> **Multi-Use Card Economy**: cards can be held in hand for synergy bonuses; staff cards expand hand capacity with ongoing costs.

## Desired change

Replace the staff description to reflect the two-type model:
> **Multi-Use Card Economy**: cards can be held in hand for synergy bonuses; staff cards come in two types — business staff (scoped to a single business) and management-company staff (player-scoped, and the only type that grants hand capacity) — both at ongoing salary costs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Engine PR merge and submodule pin update are separate steps; if the engine repo's CI is down, the submodule pin in this repo cannot be advanced until the PR merges.
- **Risk:** The engine repo may have its own work-item tracking — an engine-level work item should be created to track the change there.
- **Assumption:** The normal practice for submodule pin updates in this repository (separate pnpm/npm bump) applies — to be confirmed at implementation time.
- **Scope creep:** No additional staff-related doc changes beyond `core/README.md` should be included; all other design docs were already fixed by the parent consistency review.

## Key Files

- `core/README.md` — The Main Street row in the example-games table (line ~350), needs staff description rewrite.
- Engine repo submodule config — `.gitmodules` references `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW2XMBD5006UV3N** — *Consistency review across all updated docs* (completed). This item discovered the stale statement in `core/README.md` as a follow-up (see finding #1 in the consistency review report at `docs/dev/staff-two-type-consistency-review.md`).
- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Parent epic *Staff impact*.
- **MS-0MW2XMAD2005MNQ4** — *Reconcile card-catalog.md with the two-type model* (completed). A child of the consistency review, part of the same two-type staff model rollout.
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** — *Core scaffold template Pages base* (completed). Unrelated match.
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — *[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe* (completed). Unrelated match.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What is the exact wording to use for the new staff description?
  A: Use the two-type model: "business staff" (scoped to a single business, effects scoped to that business and its 8-way neighbours) and "management-company staff" (player-scoped, only type that grants hand capacity). Both incur ongoing salary costs. This is consistent with the GDD Appendix D.4 model documented across all design docs. Source: consistency review report, `docs/dev/staff-two-type-consistency-review.md`.

- Q: How should the submodule pin be updated after merging?
  A: Follow the normal practice used for other submodule pin updates in this repository (separate pnpm/npm bump if required). The consistency review did not document the exact mechanism — this will be determined when the engine PR is merged.

# Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger

## Problem statement

The end-of-turn ledger (the Turn Summary dialog) displays financial figures
without explaining how those figures were derived. Players see rows such as
`Business income: +42` or `Staff costs: -8` but have no way to understand how
the totals were computed, which businesses contributed, or what factors
influenced the amounts. This makes it hard to learn the economy or to plan the
next turn.

## Users

- **The human player** — needs to understand their turn's financial outcome to
  make strategic decisions for the next turn.
- **Competitive seats (AI/human)** — the per-seat tabbed panel should expose the
  same breakdowns for the selected seat.

### User stories

- _As a player, I want to hover over each ledger line to see a tooltip that
  explains exactly how that line is calculated, so I can understand my
  financial position._
- _As a player, when I hover over "Business income" I want to see a breakdown
  of each business owned and the amount coming from each, so I can understand
  where my income comes from._
- _As a player, when I hover over "Incident" I want to see which event caused
  it and what the effect was, so I can understand the impact._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every row of the Turn Summary P&L statement — each income line, each
   expense line, the Incident row, the One-off row and the Net profit/loss
   bottom line — displays an explanation tooltip on hover (desktop) and on tap
   (touch), using the shared `attachHudTooltipZone` / `tooltipManager` pattern.
2. The "Business income" tooltip (base/synergy/revenue income lines) breaks
   down each business owned, showing the business name and its individual coin
   contribution.
3. The "Staff costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual staff
   card.
4. The "Community costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual
   community space.
5. The "Business costs" tooltip breaks down the running cost of each individual
   business card.
6. The "Incident" tooltip shows the incident card name and describes its coin
   and reputation effect.
7. The "One-off" tooltip explains the source of the one-off adjustment (market
   purchases/sales, event plays, Community Favour, etc.), or, where a per-source
   breakdown is not available, the reconciliation formula that produces it.
8. The "Net profit/loss" tooltip explains the reconciliation formula:
   income + expenses + incident + one-off = net.
9. Supplementary context rows (reputation change, score change, closing coins,
   businesses owned) also display tooltips explaining their derivation.
10. Tooltip content is localisable via the existing i18n system (`t()` /
    `registerLocale`), with English defaults registered at module load.
11. Tooltips are non-blocking: they appear on hover/tap and dismiss on
    mouse-out/second tap without interfering with tab switching or the
    `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]` buttons.
12. Competitive closings render the same tooltips for the selected seat's tab.
13. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
    comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
14. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can now see exactly how every figure in the end-of-turn ledger is
calculated — which businesses earn the most, what costs drag them down, and
how incidents and one-offs affected the bottom line.

## Constraints

- Tooltips must be purely presentational: no new state mutations and no RNG
  consumption.
- Tooltips follow the existing visual style (dark background, gold accent for
  headings, readable font size) consistent with the Turn Summary dialog.
- No new accounting data invented by the UI: tooltips present figures the
  engine already commits (or expose an existing per-item breakdown), so the
  statement still reconciles to `TurnLedger`.
- The existing `TurnLedger`/`CompetitiveRoundLedger` shapes carry per-phase and
  per-category subtotals but not per-item detail; per-item data must be either
  threaded from the engine or derived from existing structures
  (`IncomeResult.breakdown`, `streetGrid` slots, `staffCards`, etc.).
- Reuse the shared tooltip helper rather than inventing a new tooltip widget.

## Existing state

- The ledger is rendered by `presentTurnSummaryPanel` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`. Rows are created by the
  `addLine` / `addHeading` helpers as non-interactive
  `Phaser.GameObjects.Text` objects.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` projects the committed ledger into a
  `PLProjection` (income lines, expense lines, incident/one-off adjustments,
  net bottom line, supplementary context) — currently `{ label, coins }`
  pairs with no per-item breakdown.
- Per-business income detail exists in `IncomeResult.breakdown`
  (`SlotIncome[]`: `businessName`, `baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) and
  in `PhaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (`SlotPhaseBreakdown`).
- Per-item ongoing costs are computed per card in
  `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` /
  `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`), but only the
  family totals reach `TurnLedger.ongoingCosts`.
- The one-off delta is currently a residual
  (`netCoinChange - incomeCoins - ongoingTotal - incidentCoinChange`), with no
  per-source breakdown stored.
- The project already has an established tooltip system:
  `attachHudTooltipZone` (`core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts`) drives
  `scene.tooltipManager` on hover/tap; `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` builds HUD
  tooltip content with i18n; `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` shows the DOM-based
  tooltip container pattern.

## Desired change

- Extend the Turn Summary model (`MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) so each
  statement/context row can carry optional per-item breakdown data (business
  name → coins, staff card → cost, community space → cost, business → cost,
  incident name → effect, one-off source → coins).
- Add i18n keys and English defaults for the new tooltip titles/bodies,
  following `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`.
- In `presentTurnSummaryPanel`, attach the shared tooltip helper to each
  `addLine` text object, building the content lazily from the model.
- Where the engine does not currently surface per-item detail (notably
  one-off sources), either thread the breakdown from the closing phase or
  present the reconciliation formula; document the choice.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — attach tooltips to ledger rows
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — add per-item breakdown fields to the
  model/projection
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — reference/owner for tooltip i18n keys
  and content builders (or a new sibling module)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — source of the ledger and (if extended)
  one-off/per-item attribution
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — per-card ongoing-cost helpers
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `SlotIncome` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown`
  income breakdowns
- `core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `attachHudTooltipZone` shared helper

## Related work

- **MS-0MW3O2O0V00042E5** – Out-of-actions dialog overlay with End Turn/Dismiss and enable checkbox (completed)
- **MS-0MUZK652V001L71C** – Player-facing win target consistency HUD tooltip help (completed)
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** – Synergy tooltip (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — mentions income, business, ledger, tooltip
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — mentions tooltips, ledger, income
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — mentions business, tooltip, income

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The existing `TurnLedger` / `IncomeResult` structures already
  contain (or can cheaply expose) the per-item data needed for tooltips. If
  not, additional data must be threaded through from the engine.
- **Assumption:** "Every line" includes the supplementary context rows;
  tooltips there are explanatory, not per-item.
- **Risk — one-off detail:** the ledger stores one-off only as a residual, so a
  true per-source breakdown needs engine work. Mitigation: present the
  reconciliation formula if threading per-source data proves invasive.
- **Risk — competitive parity:** competitive closings use
  `CompetitiveRoundLedger`, whose per-seat detail may differ; tooltips must
  degrade gracefully when a breakdown is unavailable.
- **Risk — performance/clutter:** tooltips on many rows could feel heavy; build
  content lazily and keep hit areas tight.
- **Risk — mobile:** tap-toggle tooltips on a modal with buttons must not
  collide with button presses (use `tapToggle: false` where the object is
  already a button).
- **Scope creep:** richer analytics (charts, per-turn history) are out of
  scope; record extra ideas as linked work items rather than expanding here.

## Assumptions communicated to producer

- A hover+tooltip is the chosen interaction (matches existing HUD tooltips).
- Supplementary context rows are included in scope.
- One-off may fall back to a formula-based explanation if a per-source
  breakdown would require invasive engine changes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should supplementary context lines (reputation change, score change,
  closing coins, businesses owned) also have tooltips?" — Answer (inferred from
  "every line"): yes; they get explanatory tooltips. Source: work-item
  description, MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO. Marked assumption, not a blocking question.
- Q: "Should tooltips work on mobile (tap-to-show) or desktop-only (hover)?" —
  Answer: both, matching the existing `attachHudTooltipZone` hover/tap pattern.
  Source: `core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts`.
- Q: "For the 'business costs' expense line, does each business incur ongoing
  costs, or is it a flat fee?" — Answer: per-business; each placed, unsold
  business card charges its own `ongoingCost` (less Cost Cutter reduction).
  Source: `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`.
- Q: "Can a per-source one-off breakdown be shown?" — Answer: not from the
  current ledger (residual only); fall back to the reconciliation formula
  unless the producer wants engine-level attribution added. Source:
  `buildTurnLedger` in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`. OPEN QUESTION if a
  true per-source breakdown is required.
data.title: Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger

# Extend staff cost-text guard for percentage-based reductions

## Summary
Extend the staff cost-reduction text/data consistency guard to detect percentage-based ongoing-cost descriptions (such as the Bookkeeper's "−20% ongoing cost") that have no backing data column.

## Background
The existing guard in `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` uses `UNREGISTERED_COST_REDUCTION_RE` which explicitly excludes percentages via a negative lookahead. The Bookkeeper's description "Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%" currently escapes this guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The guard detects percentage-based ongoing-cost descriptions that have no backing data column.
2. The Bookkeeper (staff-bookkeeper) is registered in the guard's contract list with `column: null` and a note linking to the Bookkeeper gap work item (MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY).
3. A new test asserts that the Bookkeeper's description triggers a guard failure when detected as unregistered.
4. All existing guard tests (6 tests) continue to pass.
5. The guard test file passes after changes.
6. **Regression guard extended:** the staff cost-text/data consistency guard (`tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts`) is extended so a percentage-based staff cost-reduction description with no backing data fails the build.

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — extend the guard to catch percentage patterns and register the Bookkeeper
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only source for the Bookkeeper description

## Dependencies
None — this child is independent.

## Notes
The percentage pattern to detect is: ongoing cost described as a percentage (e.g. "by 20%") with no corresponding backing data column in the CSV.
data.title: Extend staff cost-text guard for percentage-based reductions

# Verification: ledger tooltip model and content

## Summary

Unit tests (vitest) that lock down the per-item breakdown data added to the
Turn Summary P&L model and the tooltip content builders that render it. This
is the verification half of the ledger-tooltip work (parent
MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO): it proves that every figure a player can hover has a
correct, localised explanation derived from committed engine data.

## Scope

Covers the model fields and content builders only. The overlay wiring
(`attachHudTooltipZone` attachment and interaction) is verified by the sibling
verification items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests assert the "Business income" tooltip breaks down each business owned, showing the business name and its individual coin contribution.
- Unit tests assert the "Staff costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual staff card.
- Unit tests assert the "Community costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual community space.
- Unit tests assert the "Business costs" tooltip breaks down the running cost of each individual business card.
- Unit tests assert the "Incident" tooltip shows the incident card name and describes its coin and reputation effect.
- Unit tests assert the "One-off" tooltip explains the source of the one-off adjustment, or the reconciliation formula that produces it where no per-source breakdown exists.
- Unit tests assert the "Net profit/loss" tooltip explains the reconciliation formula: income + expenses + incident + one-off = net.
- Tooltip content is asserted to be localisable via the existing i18n system (`t()` / `registerLocale`), with English defaults registered at module load.
- Tests live under `tests/main-street/` in vitest style and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Implementation

- Add `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts`.
- Build fixtures from `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState` with
  known businesses, staff cards and community spaces so every expected number
  is exact.
- Assert exact content strings rather than snapshot blobs, so the test states
  the contract rather than baking in incidental formatting.
- Cover the absent-breakdown path (legacy/hand-built ledger) explicitly.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip content`
  (the feature that adds the fields and builders these tests verify).

## Deliverables

- New vitest test file covering every tooltip content builder and the
  breakdown model.

# Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip content

## Summary

Add optional per-item breakdown data to the Turn Summary P&L projection and
build the localised tooltip content that renders it — the data-and-copy half
of the ledger tooltip work.

## Context

The ledger already commits family totals (`TurnLedger.incomeByPhase`,
`TurnLedger.ongoingCosts`) but the per-item detail lives elsewhere:

- `IncomeResult.breakdown` (`SlotIncome[]`) and
  `PhaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` carry per-business income;
- `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` /
  `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` compute per-card costs, but only the family
  totals reach `TurnLedger.ongoingCosts`;
- the one-off delta is a residual with no per-source breakdown stored.

This feature threads the available detail into the projection and records the
documented fallback where engine detail does not exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The "Business income" tooltip (base/synergy/revenue income lines) breaks down each business owned, showing the business name and its individual coin contribution.
- The "Staff costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual staff card.
- The "Community costs" tooltip breaks down the cost of each individual community space.
- The "Business costs" tooltip breaks down the running cost of each individual business card.
- The "Incident" tooltip shows the incident card name and describes its coin and reputation effect.
- The "One-off" tooltip explains the source of the one-off adjustment (market purchases/sales, event plays, Community Favour, etc.), or, where a per-source breakdown is not available, the reconciliation formula that produces it; the chosen fallback is documented in code and in the game docs.
- The "Net profit/loss" tooltip explains the reconciliation formula: income + expenses + incident + one-off = net.
- Supplementary context rows (reputation change, score change, closing coins, businesses owned) carry the derivation data their tooltips need.
- Tooltip content is localisable via the existing i18n system (`t()` / `registerLocale`), with English defaults registered at module load.
- No new accounting data is invented by the UI: every presented figure reconciles to `TurnLedger` / `CompetitiveRoundLedger`, and no state or RNG is touched.

## Implementation

- Extend `PLStatementLine`, `PLAdjustmentLine` and `PLSupplementaryContext`
  (and their `TurnSummary*Row` sources) with optional breakdown fields.
  Keep them absent-safe so legacy and hand-built ledgers still render.
- Widen `buildTurnSummary` / `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` to accept the
  per-item sources (`TurnResult.income`, `TurnResult.playerIncome`) and
  populate the breakdowns. Widening the `Pick<...>` types keeps existing
  callers source-compatible.
- Derive per-card ongoing costs from `streetGrid` / `staffCards` / community
  spaces when the engine does not expose them; mirror the engine's own
  `ongoingCost` calculation (including the Cost Cutter reduction) rather than
  reimplementing it.
- Add a ledger-tooltip i18n key set and content builders alongside
  `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (a new sibling module if that file is already at
  its cohesion limit), following its `t()` + `registerLocale` pattern.
- Keep the one-off fallback to the reconciliation formula when no per-source
  detail exists; document the choice in a TSDoc comment.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`

## Dependencies

- None (first implementation feature).

## Deliverables

- Extended P&L model with per-item breakdowns (absent-safe).
- Localised tooltip content builders with English defaults.
- Documented one-off fallback decision.
data.title: Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip content

# Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows

## Summary

Make every Turn Summary P&L row and supplementary context row interactive:
hover on desktop, tap on touch, dismissing cleanly without disturbing the
panel's tabs and buttons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every row of the Turn Summary P&L statement — each income line, each expense line, the Incident row, the One-off row and the Net profit/loss bottom line — displays an explanation tooltip on hover (desktop) and on tap (touch), using the shared `attachHudTooltipZone` / `tooltipManager` pattern.
- Supplementary context rows (reputation change, score change, closing coins, businesses owned) also display tooltips explaining their derivation.
- Tooltips are non-blocking: they appear on hover/tap and dismiss on mouse-out/second tap without interfering with tab switching or the `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]` buttons.
- Tooltip content is built lazily from the projection, so no content strings are computed for rows the player never hovers.
- Hit areas stay tight to each row's own text, so adjacent rows and the panel's controls keep working.
- Tooltips are purely presentational: no new state mutations and no RNG consumption.

## Implementation

- Thread an optional content-builder argument through the overlay's internal
  `addLine` helper and call `attachHudTooltipZone` for each row.
- Rebuild the tooltip closures on each `draw()` so a tab switch shows the
  selected seat's content (the panel already redraws on `selectTab`).
- Use `tapToggle: false` where a row is also a control; hover-only there.
- Keep the dark-background / gold-accent styling consistent with the dialog by
  reusing the existing tooltip manager configuration.
- Track every tooltip-bearing object in `s.overlayObjects` so `dismissOverlay`
  releases them with the rest of the panel.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`
- `core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip content`.

## Deliverables

- Interactive ledger rows with hover/tap tooltips.
- Lazy content construction with tight hit areas and clean teardown.
data.title: Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows

# Competitive per-seat tooltip parity

## Summary

Give competitive closings the same ledger tooltips for the selected seat's
tab, degrading gracefully where `CompetitiveRoundLedger` carries no per-item
detail.

## Context

Competitive closings project through `CompetitiveTurnSummary` /
`CompetitiveRoundLedger`, whose per-seat detail differs from the single-player
`TurnLedger`. `OwnerRoundLedger` carries `incomeByPhase` and `ongoingCosts`
subtotals but not per-item rows, so a seat's tooltip may have less to say than
the human seat's in single-player. The panel must never show a wrong or empty
breakdown.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Competitive closings render the same tooltips for the selected seat's tab as the single-player panel renders for the human seat.
- Per-seat income and expense tooltips use the seat's own breakdowns, and switching tabs switches the tooltip content.
- Where a seat's ledger carries no per-item breakdown (older or hand-built `CompetitiveRoundLedger`), the tooltip shows the category total plus an explanatory note instead of a wrong or empty breakdown.
- Tooltip rendering for non-human seats never mutates state or consumes RNG.
- The human seat's tooltips match the single-player wording and i18n keys exactly.

## Implementation

- Populate per-seat breakdowns in `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` from
  `result.playerIncome` where present (`OwnerIncomeResult.income.breakdown`),
  keeping the fields optional.
- Reuse the same content builders as the single-player path; pass
  `undefined` to trigger the graceful category-total fallback.
- Re-attach tooltips on each tab switch — the panel already redraws the whole
  statement body on `selectTab`.
- Widen the overlay's competitive `result` parameter to include
  `playerIncome` so the refresh path keeps the breakdowns after a loan take.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows`.

## Deliverables

- Competitive per-seat tooltips with graceful degradation.
- Tab-switch re-attachment preserving correct content.

## Plan complete — feature decomposition

Decomposed MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO into 7 children: 3 verification items (created
first, test-first ordering) and 4 implementation features. Execution order is
driven by dependency edges: `Extend P&L model...` → `Attach tooltips...` →
`Competitive per-seat tooltip parity` → `Documentation...`; each verification
item depends on the feature it verifies so no red-test commit is ever needed
(the build → test → commit gate holds).

### Children

| # | Work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|-----------|------|------------|
| 1 | Verification: ledger tooltip model and content (MS-0MW7QQ1FD000RCA3) | task | F1 |
| 2 | Verification: overlay tooltip attachment (MS-0MW7QQ1TV009I4G9) | task | F2 |
| 3 | Verification: browser tooltip behaviour (MS-0MW7QQ286007L4J3) | task | F3 |
| 4 | Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip content (MS-0MW7QQ5BX002KGS0) | feature | — |
| 5 | Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows (MS-0MW7QQ5QU007XXC0) | feature | F1 |
| 6 | Competitive per-seat tooltip parity (MS-0MW7QQ65P006N3KA) | feature | F2 |
| 7 | Documentation for ledger tooltips (MS-0MW7QQ6KC006S5E8) | docs | F3 |

### Vertical-slice phasing

Each implementation feature is a thin end-to-end slice: F1 carries model +
engine-data threading + localised content (testable without a browser); F2
carries the user-visible overlay interaction; F3 carries competitive parity;
F4 carries docs. Between phases the implementer reviews the next item's
description and updates it if the engine data proves different from the
prediction.

### Six automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: mapped all 14 parent ACs onto the
children (AC1→F2/T2, AC2–AC8→F1/T1, AC9→F2/T2, AC10→F1/T1, AC11→F2/T2,
AC12→F3/T3, AC13→F4, AC14→every verification item). No invented or
contradictory ACs.

Finished Completeness review: every child has Summary, ACs, Implementation,
Key Files, Dependencies and Deliverables; Key Files paths carry a directory
separator and an extension; no missing fields.

Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: no cycles; test/verification items
are listed first and each is wired to the feature it verifies; implementation
order is model → overlay → competitive → docs.

Finished Scope sizing review: all feats sized as deliverable increments
(largest is F1 at roughly the WBS's model + content items); no feature mixes
unrelated concerns.

Finished Acceptance & testability review: every AC is a pass/fail check
(named row, named figure, named formula, named test file); the one-off AC
explicitly allows the reconciliation-formula fallback.

Finished Polish & handoff review: descriptions are copy-pasteable, use UK
English, and name the exact files and helpers an implementer needs.

### AC coverage review

`apply_coverage_review` → `proceed`; all 14 parent ACs covered (100%),
0 unresolved conflicts, 0 auto-closed gaps.

### Appendix: questions

No new producer questions arose: the intake Appendix already answers the
blocking uncertainties — the one-off residual may fall back to the
reconciliation formula (explicitly permitted by parent AC7 and the "Desired
change" section), supplementary context rows are in scope, and the
hover/tap interaction follows the existing `attachHudTooltipZone` pattern.
No requirement was invented.

### Assumptions carried into implementation

- Per-item ongoing costs can be derived from `streetGrid` / `staffCards` /
  community spaces when the engine does not surface them; if that proves
  invasive, F1 falls back to the category total (already permitted).
- `TurnResult.income.breakdown` and `TurnResult.playerIncome` are the
  authoritative per-business income sources.
- Competitive per-seat breakdowns may be absent; the tooltip degrades to the
  category total with an explanatory note.
